title: Evidence for Evolution
seo_title: Evidence for Evolution Worksheets: Fossils, Anatomy and DNA (High School Biology)
standard_text: Communicate scientific information that common ancestry and biological evolution are supported by multiple lines of empirical evidence.
meta_desc: Free high school biology worksheets on evidence for evolution (NGSS HS-LS4-1): homologous and vestigial structures, fossils, rock layers and DNA comparisons. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Many lines of evidence show common ancestry.
key_sub: Fossils, anatomy, embryos and DNA all point to the same family tree.
body_html:
How to think about it

Many lines of evidence show common ancestry.

  • Anatomy: homologous structures (same bones, different jobs) and vestigial structures. Analogous structures do not show close relationship.
  • Fossils: lower layers are older; transitional fossils mix traits of two groups.
  • DNA and proteins: fewer differences mean a more recent common ancestor.
Example

Chimpanzee: 1 difference. Tuna: 21. Closer to humans?

Fewer differences = closer

Answer: chimpanzee

Example

Human arm and whale flipper have the same bones. What kind?

Same bones, different jobs

Answer: homologous

Common mistakes

  • Thinking similar jobs (bird and insect wings) mean close relatives.
  • Saying humans evolved from chimpanzees.
  • Thinking more differences mean a closer relative.

faq.q: What are the main lines of evidence for evolution?
faq.a: The fossil record, comparative anatomy (homologous and vestigial structures), embryology and DNA or protein sequences.

faq.q: How do DNA comparisons show relationships?
faq.a: Species with fewer differences in their DNA or proteins share a more recent common ancestor.

faq.q: What is the difference between homologous and analogous structures?
faq.a: Homologous structures have the same bones from a common ancestor. Analogous structures do the same job but evolved separately.

items.q: What kind of structures are these: a penguin flipper and a fish fin?
items.e: Same job, different build: no close common ancestor.

items.q: Which fossil shows the change from fish to four-legged land animals?
c: early horse fossils such as Eohippus
items.e: It has traits of both groups.

items.q: What are homologous structures?
c: body parts with similar bones because of a shared ancestor
parts that do the same job in unrelated species

items.q: What is a common ancestor?
c: an earlier species that two or more living species evolved from
a species alive today that others came from

items.q: Why do scientists count the human tailbone as evidence for evolution?
c: Such parts prove the species never changed.
Such parts are new and will be used later.
Such parts do the same job as in all relatives.
Such reduced parts are leftovers of structures that were useful in ancestors.

items.q: What kind of structures are these: the human tailbone?
items.e: Reduced and little or no use now.

items.q: Scientists compare a bat wing and a bee wing. They do the same job but are built very differently. What does this suggest?
c: The two species share a recent common ancestor.
They evolved separately in similar environments.
items.e: Analogous structures come from similar needs, not shared ancestry.

items.q: What are vestigial structures?
c: reduced body parts with little or no use now
parts that do the same job

items.q: Why are early embryos of fish, chickens and humans similar?
c: They will become the same animal.
They share a common ancestor and early developmental genes.

items.q: Which fossil shows the change from dinosaurs to birds?
c: early horse fossils such as Eohippus
items.e: It has traits of both groups.

items.q: Which evidence uses DNA or proteins to compare species?
Did humans evolve from chimpanzees?
c: No, they are not related at all.
No. Humans and chimpanzees share a common ancestor.

items.q: What does the principle of superposition say?
c: In undisturbed rock layers, lower layers are older.
All layers are the same age.

items.q: Fossils of Tiktaalik show fins with wrist-like bones, a neck and lungs. They are evidence of which change?
c: from fish to four-legged land animals
from small forest animals to modern one-toed horses
items.e: A transitional fossil mixes old and new traits.

items.q: Which fossil shows the change from land mammals to whales?
c: early horse fossils such as Eohippus
items.e: It has traits of both groups.

items.q: Why is evolution accepted by scientists?
c: Many independent lines of evidence point to the same conclusions.
items.e: Fossils, anatomy, embryos and DNA agree.
